favored: banks/financials -- elevated T-bill/PIB cutoffs (6M 11.80%, 10Y PIB 12.30%) remain a genuine carry tailwind for balance sheets holding government paper, with the held policy rate at 11.5% preserving that spread into the Sept 14 MPC; BOP's +44% 1HCY26 profit print (this checkpoint's trigger) is a data point supporting this tilt for large, well-capitalized names -- it does not extend to small/distressed banks like BML
E&P/OMC -- soft oil (Brent $87.53, -0.94% 1mo per global.json) keeps input costs benign for OMCs, while upstream names benefit from a still-elevated absolute price level

exporters/textiles -- July's export rebound to a 19-month high ($3.0bn) and the narrowing current-account deficit are a genuine external-balance tailwind, though the trend needs the August print to confirm it is durable rather than a one-month bounce
avoid: power/IPP names exposed to the circular-debt overhang -- Pakistan missed its FY26 circular-debt reduction target (Rs1.835tn actual vs Rs1.614tn commitment) and the IMF's September review mission has electricity/gas tariff pass-through and circular-debt reform as the key unresolved sticking point

small/thinly-capitalized banks with idiosyncratic balance-sheet stress -- Bank Makramah's swing to a Rs4.68bn 1HCY26 loss (this checkpoint's trigger) and its prior Rs10bn sponsor-injection need (2026-08-18, per state/georisk.json) illustrate the dispersion within the sector; the carry tailwind above applies to large banks holding government paper, not distressed names
